whitespace_angles.angle: Catalog data quality is the wrong bottleneck — Glance's D0 feed sidesteps it entirely
whitespace_angles.why_glance: The Agentic Commerce Frontier found <1% of product pages meet LLM-ready thresholds, and the whole industry is racing to fix merchant catalog data. Glance's Brand AI Store partners submit curated assets directly — no page scraping, no LLM parsing of badly structured PDFs. The bottleneck that is killing agent commerce for everyone else doesn't exist in the D0 model.

whitespace_angles.angle: OpenAI paused Instant Checkout — what the trust gap means for ambient commerce
whitespace_angles.why_glance: OpenAI quietly paused its Instant Checkout feature in early May 2026. Coverage treats this as a trust calibration problem. Nobody has written the counter-angle: the D0 lockscreen card shows the user the product before any tap is required — it is inherently a higher-trust surface than a chatbot completing checkout in the background.

whitespace_angles.angle: UCP coalition now includes Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce — and still no OEM layer
whitespace_angles.why_glance: The Universal Commerce Protocol tech council added Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Salesforce this week alongside Google, Shopify, and Wayfair. Every major platform is now in UCP — except OEM-embedded surfaces. The coalition covers every app layer but misses the device layer entirely. Glance operates at the device layer and requires no protocol membership to surface products.

whitespace_angles.angle: FIDO Agent Trust frameworks vs. OEM pre-consent — why the registration layer is unnecessary on Glance
whitespace_angles.why_glance: FIDO and Experian are building 'Agent Trust' frameworks that require agents to register, get credentials, and prove identity before acting on behalf of users. Glance's OEM pre-consent model is more fundamental: Glance is baked into the device at manufacture, with consent negotiated once at the OS level. No registration needed. The trust frameworks everyone is building solve a problem that the OEM layer doesn't have.

whitespace_angles.angle: Stablecoins for agentic settlement: the infrastructure play nobody needs at Glance
whitespace_angles.why_glance: Multiple newsletters (insights4vc, Robonomics) are bullish on stablecoins as the native settlement layer for machine-to-machine commerce. The argument is that card networks are too slow and expensive for micro-agent transactions. Glance's lockscreen commerce operates over Stripe/UPI rails with human-initiated tap-to-buy — no machine-to-machine settlement needed. This is a non-problem for D0 surfaces.

whitespace_angles.angle: Google I/O agentic booking (flights, hotels, restaurants in AI Mode) — and what it doesn't cover
whitespace_angles.why_glance: Google I/O 2026 is expected to announce agentic booking directly in AI Mode — book a flight or restaurant without leaving Search. Coverage will frame this as the end of the booking funnel. What won't be covered: the discovery moment before the user types any query. Glance's D0 feed can surface a restaurant or flight recommendation at device wake, before the user even opens Google.

momentum_angles.angle: Catalog data quality / 'AI-readiness' for merchant storefronts
momentum_angles.coverage_summary: Mirakl data showing <1% of product pages meet LLM-ready thresholds is generating widespread coverage. The narrative: merchants must restructure their catalog data or become invisible to AI agents. Tooling companies (Feedonomics, ReFiBuy) are capitalising.
momentum_angles.glance_counter_angle: Catalog AI-readiness is a problem for pull-based agents. Glance's D0 feed uses curated first-party brand assets — no scraping, no LLM parsing, no threshold to fail. The 99% problem doesn't apply.

momentum_angles.angle: UCP coalition expansion and protocol standardisation
momentum_angles.coverage_summary: UCP added Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce this week. The protocol is becoming the de facto standard for agent-mediated retail transactions across every major platform. Merchant integration guides are proliferating.
momentum_angles.glance_counter_angle: UCP covers the transaction layer. Glance owns the discovery layer that precedes any UCP transaction — a layer that UCP by design cannot address because it requires a user session to exist first.

momentum_angles.angle: Google I/O 2026 as inflection point for agentic AI
momentum_angles.coverage_summary: Google I/O 2026 (May 19-20) is treated as the moment Gemini-native commerce goes mainstream: agentic booking in AI Mode, UCP Buy Button in Search, Gemini Spark '24/7 personal agent', Android XR glasses. Every publication is framing this as the tipping point.
momentum_angles.glance_counter_angle: Everything Google is announcing at I/O requires Search to be open. Glance's D0 surfaces recommendations before Search is launched. Google I/O is the best possible moment to publish 'What Google Can't Do From the Lockscreen.'
